The insurance company of the vehicle in question challenges the award passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Additional District Judge, Hosur in M.C.O.P.No.247 of 2018.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2.Notice to the fourth respondent is not necessary since the appellant only challenges the quantum awarded by the Tribunal.
3.A certain Reddy sekar, a driver of the tractor belonging to the fourth respondent herein had died when the tractor capsized.
Seeking compensation, the dependants of the victim approached the Tribunal, and the Tribunal had awarded a sum of Rs.16,37,000/- as compensation.

In the process, it rejected the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis contention of the insurance company that the accident has occasioned due to the negligence of the victim and as a tortfeasor, the claimants are not entitled to any compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
This part of the award is now under challenge.

The breakup of the award is as below:
 Sl.No Heads Amount awarded  . Tribunal  1. Loss of dependency Rs.10,80,
 2. Loss of love and affection Rs.45,0  3. Transportation Rs.10,0  4. Funeral expenses Rs.15,0  5. Loss of estate Rs.15,0  6. Loss of consortium Rs.40,0  7. Loss of future prospects Rs.4,32,

Total Rs.16,37,
4.Heard Mr.G.Vasudevan, the learned counsel for the appellant and Mr.C.Prabakaran, the learned counsel appearing for respondents 1 and 2.
5.The learned counsel for the appellant submitted along the lines of his contention it had taken before the Tribunal that there can be no compensation if https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the victim himself is a tortfeasor, which is not in dispute.

6.There are two options before this Court now: (a) under Section 164 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, if evoked, the claimants will be entitled to Rs.5 Lakhs; (b) to workout the remedy under the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 since the victim admittedly was an employee of the fourth respondent herein.

Since the Workmen's Compensation Act provides additional benefit to the The Manager vs K.Kosuri Kumari on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88058940/
2 claimants, this Court considers it appropriate.
7.Here, this Court encounters a problem in procedure, therefore, this case is converted into one under Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923.

The following substantial questions of law is framed:
"When the victim of the accident is an employee of the insured, is it permissible for the Tribunal to award compensation under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles act when the victim himself was a tortfeasor."
8 . A s a l r e a d y i n d i c a t e d , t h e c l a i m a n t s d e f i n i t e l y w o u l d b e e n t i t l e d t o https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis compensation under the Employees Compensation Act, 1923.
The victim was 39 years old at the relevant time.
Therefore, the notional income of the victim is fixed at Rs.8,000/- per month.

The appropriate multiplicand age factor is 186.90, so calculated, the compensation would be as below:
 Heads Award   (Amou  Loss of Income (Rs.8,000/- x 186.90 x 50/100) 
 Funeral Expenses   Total  9.In
the result
, this appeal stands partly allowed, and the total compensation to which the claimants are entitled to is determined at Rs.7,52,600/-.

The appellant is now directed to deposit the balance amount, less than the amount if any already deposited with interest at 12% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of six (6) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit being made, the respondents 1, 3 and 4 are permitted to withdraw the amount awarded by this Court which is N.SESHASAYEE, J.
A n u r e q u i r e d t o b e a p p o r t i o n e d i n t h e s a m e r a t i o i n w h i c h t h e T r i b u n a l h a s
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

apportioned the compensation, along with proportionate interest,
less, the amount, if any already withdrawn.
The amount due to the minor / the second respondent shall be deposited in a Nationalized Bank.
Till the minor attains majority, the quarterly interest can be withdrawn by the first respondent for the maintenance of the minor.
No Costs.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
